senses.definition: (countable, uncountable) A visible fact that shows that something exists or may happen.
examples: Their angry expressions were a clear sign they didn't want to talk.
Those clouds show signs of raining soon.
Those clouds show little sign of raining soon.

quotes.text: Although the Celebrity was almost impervious to sarcasm, he was now beginning to exhibit visible signs of uneasiness, the consciousness dawning upon him that his eccentricity was not receiving the ovation it merited.
quotes.reference: 1897 December (indicated as 1898), Winston Churchill, chapter V, in The Celebrity: An Episode, New York, N.Y.: The Macmillan Company; London: Macmillan & Co., Ltd., →OCLC:

quotes.text: No, I don't know why you're not fair / I give you my love, but you don't care / So what is right and what is wrong? / Gimme a sign
quotes.reference: 1993 January 18, Dee Dee Halligan, Junior Torello, “What Is Love”, in The Album, performed by Haddaway:

examples: "It's a sign of the end of the world," the doom prophet said.

subsenses.definition: (medicine) A property of the body that indicates a disease and, unlike a symptom, can be detected objectively by someone other than the patient.
examples: Signs of disease are objective, whereas symptoms are subjective.

senses.definition: A mark or another symbol used to represent something.
examples: The sharp sign indicates that the pitch of the note is raised a half step.
I gave them a thumbs-up sign.

quotes.text: The sound of the Orlando dinner train whistle reminds me that it ' s already Friday, an auditory sign. Another auditory sign, a distant thunder clap, warns me of limited computer time before our evening thunderstorm moves in.

senses.definition: (Canada, US, Australia, uncountable) Physical evidence left by an animal.
examples: The hunters found deer sign at the end of the trail.

quotes.text: Animal sign is the key to eliminating guesswork when setting your traps. Only trap where there is sign. Sign is anything the animal leaves as a trace that indicates it may have passed through the area.
quotes.reference: 2015, Dave Canterbury, Advanced Bushcraft: An Expert Field Guide to the Art of Wilderness Survival, page 127:

senses.definition: A clearly visible object, generally flat, bearing a short message in words or pictures.
examples: The sign in the window advertised a room for rent.
I missed the sign at the corner so I took the wrong turn.

quotes.text: The shops were, therefore, distinguished by painted signs, which gave a gay and grotesque aspect to the streets.

senses.definition: (mathematics) Positive or negative polarity, as denoted by the + or - sign.
examples: I got the magnitude right, but the sign was wrong.

senses.definition: A specific gesture or motion used to communicate by those with speaking or hearing difficulties; now specifically, a linguistic unit in sign language equivalent to word in spoken languages.

quotes.text: And why not, as well as our dumbe men dispute, argue and tell histories by signes?

quotes.text: In American Sign Language (ASL), for instance, the sign for 'catch' is formed with one hand (in the role of agent) moving across the body (an action) to grasp the forefinger of the other hand (the patient).

senses.definition: A semantic unit, something that conveys meaning or information (e.g. a word of written language); (linguistics, semiotics) a unit consisting of a signifier and a signified concept. (See sign (semiotics).)

quotes.text: A Noun substantive and a Noun adjective may be thus distinguished, that a substantive may have the sign a or the before it; as, puer, a boy, the boy; but an adjective cannot, as, bonus, good.

quotes.text: And some linguistic signs, like “the”, “and” or “with”, may lack apparent objects, though they are clearly meaningful and interpretable.

subsenses.definition: (transitive, now rare) To seal (a document etc.) with an identifying seal or symbol.
examples: The Queen signed her letter with the regal signet.

subsenses.definition: (transitive) More generally, to write one's signature on (something) as a means of identification etc.
examples: I forgot to sign that letter to my aunt.

subsenses.definition: (transitive or reflexive) To write (one's name) as a signature.
examples: Just sign your name at the bottom there.
I received a letter from some woman who signs herself ‘Mrs Trellis’.
Please sign on the dotted line.

subsenses.definition: (intransitive) To finalise a contractual agreement to work for a given sports team, record label etc.
examples: Agents say Wales back Gavin Henson has signed for Cardiff Blues.

subsenses.definition: (transitive) To engage (a sports player, musician etc.) in a contract.
examples: It was a great month. I managed to sign three major players.
